# 2 Samuel Chapter 15 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 185r–186r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_015_page_001.jpg, 2SA_015_page_002.jpg, 2SA_015_page_003.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** After this, Absalom provided for himself a chariot and horses, and fifty men to run before him.

**2** Absalom would rise early and stand beside the road at the gate. When any man had a dispute to bring before the king for judgment, Absalom would call to him and say, "What city are you from?" And the man would say, "Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel."

**3** Absalom would say to him, "See, your claims are good and right, but there is no one appointed by the king to hear you."

**4** Then Absalom would say, "Oh that someone would appoint me judge in the land! Then every man who has a dispute or a grievance could come to me, and I would give him justice."

**5** And whenever a man came near to bow down to him, he would reach out his hand and take hold of him and kiss him.

**6** Thus Absalom did to all of Israel who came to the king for judgment. So Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.

**7** At the end of four years, Absalom said to the king, "Please let me go and pay my vow that I have vowed to the LORD, in Hebron.

**8** For your servant made a vow while I lived in Geshur in Aram, saying, 'If the LORD will indeed bring me back to Jerusalem, then I will serve the LORD.'"

**9** The king said to him, "Go in peace." So he arose and went to Hebron.

**10** But Absalom sent secret messengers throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, then say, 'Absalom has become king in Hebron!'"

**11** With Absalom went two hundred men from Jerusalem who had been invited and went in their innocence, knowing nothing of the matter.

**12** And while offering the sacrifices, Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counselor, from his city Giloh. The conspiracy grew strong, and the people with Absalom kept increasing.

**13** A messenger came to David, saying, "The hearts of the men of Israel have gone after Absalom."

**14** Then David said to all his servants who were with him at Jerusalem, "Arise, let us flee, or there will be no escape for us from Absalom. Go quickly, lest he overtake us and bring down ruin upon us and strike the city with the edge of the sword."

**15** The king's servants said to the king, "Whatever my lord the king decides, your servants are ready."

**16** So the king went out, and all his household after him, on foot. The king left ten concubines to keep the house.

**17** The king went out, and all the people after him on foot, and they halted at the last house.

**18** All his servants passed by him, and all the Cherethites and all the Pelethites, and all the six hundred Gittites who had followed him from Gath passed before the king.

**19** Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, "Why do you also come with us? Go back and stay with the king, for you are a foreigner and also an exile from your own home.

**20** You came only yesterday, and shall I today make you wander about with us, since I go I know not where? Go back and take your brothers with you. May the LORD show you covenant-faithfulness and truth."

**21** But Ittai answered the king, "As the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king shall be, whether for death or for life, there also will your servant be."

**22** David said to Ittai, "Go then, march on." So Ittai the Gittite marched on with all his men and all the little ones who were with him.

**23** All the land wept aloud as all the people passed by. The king crossed the brook Kidron, and all the people passed on toward the wilderness road.

**24** And behold, Zadok came also, with all the Levites, bearing the ark of the covenant of God. They set down the ark of God until all the people had finished passing out of the city, and Abiathar came up.

**25** Then the king said to Zadok, "Carry the ark of God back into the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the LORD, he will bring me back and let me see both it and his dwelling place.

**26** But if he says, 'I have no delight in you,' behold, here I am — let him do to me what seems good in his eyes."

**27** The king also said to Zadok the priest, "Are you not a seer? Return to the city in peace, with your two sons — Ahimaaz your son and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.

**28** See, I will wait at the fords of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me."

**29** So Zadok and Abiathar carried the ark of God back to Jerusalem, and they remained there.

**30** But David went up the ascent of the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went, with his head covered and walking barefoot. And all the people who were with him covered their heads, and they went up weeping as they went.

**31** And it was told David, "Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom." And David said, "O LORD, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness."

**32** When David came to the summit, where God was worshiped, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his robe torn and earth upon his head.

**33** David said to him, "If you pass on with me, you will be a burden to me.

**34** But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, 'I will be your servant, O king; as I was your father's servant in time past, so now I will be your servant,' then you will defeat for me the counsel of Ahithophel.

**35** Are not Zadok and Abiathar the priests with you there? Whatever you hear from the king's house, report it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.

**36** Behold, their two sons are with them there — Ahimaaz the son of Zadok and Jonathan the son of Abiathar. By them you shall send me every word that you hear."

**37** So Hushai, David's friend, came into the city just as Absalom was entering Jerusalem.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agree on the chapter's dramatic arc: Absalom's political campaign (vv.1-6), the Hebron conspiracy (vv.7-12), David's flight from Jerusalem (vv.13-23), the ark episode and David's submission to YHWH (vv.24-29), the Mount of Olives ascent (vv.30-31), and the Hushai counter-intelligence mission (vv.32-37). The theological center of the chapter — David's words to Zadok in vv.25-26 — is handled with remarkable consistency across all three translations. The textual issue of "forty years" vs. "four years" in v.7 is resolved unanimously in favor of "four years."

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.1 — "provided for himself" vs. "made for himself" vs. "got himself"
- **EMET:** "made for-himself Avshalom a-chariot"
- **LOGOS:** "Absalom provided for himself a chariot"
- **PNEUMA:** "Absalom got himself a chariot"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Absalom provided for himself a chariot." The Hebrew *vaya'as lo* is literally "he made/prepared for himself." LOGOS's "provided for himself" captures the deliberate, preparatory nature of the act without PNEUMA's colloquialism.

### V.3 — "a hearer there is not" vs. "no one appointed" vs. "the king hasn't appointed anyone"
- **EMET:** "a-hearer there-is-not to-you from the-king"
- **LOGOS:** "there is no one appointed by the king to hear you"
- **PNEUMA:** "the king hasn't appointed anyone to hear cases like yours"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "there is no one appointed by the king to hear you." LOGOS clarifies the Hebrew idiom while maintaining the formal register. PNEUMA's "cases like yours" adds specificity not in the text.

### V.7 — "forty years" vs. "four years"
- **EMET:** "forty years" (notes LC reading, acknowledges likely scribal error)
- **LOGOS:** "four years" (follows Syriac/LXX/Josephus)
- **PNEUMA:** "four years"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "four years." The MT reads "forty" (*arba'im*) but this creates a chronological impossibility. Following the Syriac Peshitta, multiple LXX manuscripts, and Josephus, the original reading was almost certainly "four" (*arba'*). The LC reading is noted.

### V.10 — "spies" vs. "secret messengers" vs. "agents"
- **EMET:** "spies [meragelim]"
- **LOGOS:** "secret messengers"
- **PNEUMA:** "agents"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "secret messengers." The Hebrew *meragelim* means "spies/scouts," but in context they function as covert messengers planting instructions. LOGOS's rendering captures the function; EMET's "spies" suggests surveillance rather than communication.

### V.14 — "drive upon us the evil" vs. "bring down ruin" vs. "bring disaster"
- **EMET:** "drive-upon-us the-evil [ra'ah]"
- **LOGOS:** "bring down ruin upon us"
- **PNEUMA:** "bring disaster on us"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "bring down ruin upon us." LOGOS captures the force and weight of *hiddiach aleinu et ha-ra'ah* more effectively than PNEUMA's flatter "bring disaster."

### V.19-20 — David's address to Ittai
- **EMET:** "I [am]-going where I [am]-going [holekh al asher ani holekh]"
- **LOGOS:** "I go I know not where"
- **PNEUMA:** "I don't even know where I'm going"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "I go I know not where." The Hebrew *holekh al asher ani holekh* is literally "going upon/to where I am going" — a deliberate vagueness. LOGOS's formal phrasing preserves the resigned uncertainty of the original. PNEUMA is accurate but too casual for the gravitas of the scene.

### V.20 — "covenant-faithfulness and truth" vs. "faithful love and truth"
- **EMET:** "Covenant-faithfulness [chesed] and-faithfulness [emet]"
- **LOGOS:** "covenant-faithfulness and truth"
- **PNEUMA:** "faithful love and truth"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "covenant-faithfulness and truth." Following the project convention for *chesed* and rendering *emet* as "truth" (its primary meaning). PNEUMA's "faithful love" is a valid rendering of *chesed* but departs from the established term.

### V.23 — "wadi of Qidron" vs. "brook Kidron" vs. "Kidron Valley"
- **EMET:** "wadi of-Qidron"
- **LOGOS:** "brook Kidron"
- **PNEUMA:** "Kidron Valley"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "brook Kidron." The Hebrew *nachal Qidron* can mean brook/wadi/valley. LOGOS's "brook" is the traditional English rendering and captures the specific watercourse David crosses.

### V.26 — "I have no delight in you" vs. "I take no pleasure in you"
- **EMET:** "Not I-have-delighted [chafatsti] in-you"
- **LOGOS:** "I have no delight in you"
- **PNEUMA:** "I take no pleasure in you"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "I have no delight in you." LOGOS preserves the starkness of the Hebrew *lo chafatsti*. PNEUMA's "take no pleasure" is close but slightly softer.

### V.28 — "plains of the wilderness" vs. "fords of the wilderness" vs. "river crossings"
- **EMET:** "plains of-the-wilderness"
- **LOGOS:** "fords of the wilderness"
- **PNEUMA:** "river crossings in the wilderness"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "fords of the wilderness." The Hebrew *aravot ha-midbar* can mean "plains/steppes" or, by context, the crossing points of the Jordan near the wilderness. LOGOS's "fords" reflects the strategic purpose — David will wait where news can reach him via the river crossing.

### V.31 — "make foolish" vs. "turn into foolishness" vs. "turn into nonsense"
- **EMET:** "Make-foolish [sakkel-na], please"
- **LOGOS:** "please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness"
- **PNEUMA:** "turn Ahithophel's advice into nonsense"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness." LOGOS preserves the *na* (please) and the formal register of prayer. PNEUMA's "nonsense" trivializes the gravity of the petition.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
